locator: M17-35 (M17.4 Requirements — tax invoice, credit note and refund)
quote: an approver, and where a refund of money follows, a link to the refund payment.
problem: "The refund payment" is referenced but never created anywhere in the specification. M17-13 lists nine payment modes and every one of them is money coming in; M17-13a then binds the Daily Collection Register and the collection-versus-remittance reconciliation to Payment records only; the M17.6 Payment field table has no outward mode, no sanction reference and no sanctioning officer; M17.7 rules 2 and 4 twice instruct staff to "refund ... with the sanction reference recorded" against a field that does not exist; M17-15 offers a status *Refunded* that no requirement ever sets; and §25.2 of section_5 holds only `txn_receipt` ("Money tendered"). Under the withdrawn assumption the LIMS raised the refund voucher and the ERP posted and paid it — the M22.1 row "Credit note and refund voucher" still shows that split. With no ERP, money leaving the laboratory has no record, no series, no authorisation and no place in any register, and the refund path the rewrite was supposed to bring in-house is only half here.
fix:
Insert this row immediately after M17-33 in M17.4:

| M17-33a | [MUST] | The system shall record every **refund of money paid out** as a **Refund Payment** in its own gap-free financial-year series, carrying: the credit note (M17-35) or refund voucher (M17-33) it discharges, as a hard link and not a free-text note; the customer; the amount; the outward mode from a controlled list (cash at the counter; demand draft; bank transfer; reversal to the instrument the money arrived on; adjustment against the customer's advance balance); the outward reference values with their types, dates and evidence files, on the same reference table as M17-14; the **sanction reference and the sanctioning officer, both mandatory**, the officer being the Approving Authority where the amount exceeds `waiver_approval_limit`; and the date the money actually left. The originating Payment moves to status *Refunded* only when a Refund Payment is committed against it, never by editing the status. A Refund Payment is money **out**: it shall never be counted as a collection in the Daily Collection Register (M17-24) or in the collection-versus-remittance reconciliation (M17-25), shall appear on both as a separate outward total, and shall post to the customer ledger (M17-21) as a debit on the date the money left. No money shall be refunded except against a committed credit note or refund voucher, and no Refund Payment shall be deleted (M17-26 applies unchanged). | Approve a credit note with a refund and attempt to pay it with the sanction reference blank; refused. Record it with the sanction reference; the originating payment reads *Refunded*, the day's collection total is unchanged, the refund shows in its own outward total, and the customer ledger carries the debit. Attempt to set a payment to *Refunded* directly; refused. |

Then add to the M17.6 Payment field table: `| Direction | In / Out | Yes | Default In; Out only on a Refund Payment (M17-33a) |`, `| Refund of payment | Link | Conditional | Required where Direction is Out; the payment being refunded |`, `| Sanction reference and sanctioning officer | Text + link to staff | Conditional | Mandatory where Direction is Out |`; add a row `| Refund payment — record / sanction | – | – | – | C | A | – | C (raise) | – | – | R own |` to the M21.3 permission matrix beside "Credit note / refund voucher"; and add `Refund Payment` to the series list in M1-68 and to §10.1 and WF-99 of section_2_workflow.md.

locator: §10.1 The series (Credit Note row) and WF-99
quote: | **Credit Note number** | `DVM/C/<FY4>/<4>` | `DVM/C/2627/0011` | Financial year | Accounts, Unit Incharge, and the customer | **Gap-free and statutory.** Must reference the invoice number and date it adjusts. |
problem: The debit note is promised in four places and specified in none. section_1_foundation.md gives Accounts the power to "Raise and issue invoices, bills of supply, receipt vouchers, credit and debit notes and refund vouchers"; M1-68 lists "Debit Note" among the series that must exist, with the acceptance check "Every document type in the list has a configured series before go-live"; §25.2 gives `txn_invoice` a `doc_type` covering "credit note, debit note"; and §26.4 puts "credit and debit note" in Phase 2 scope. But §10.1 defines no debit-note format, the sixteen-character sentence names only five length-constrained series, WF-99 omits it from the gap-free list, M17.4 contains no requirement for it, M17.1 has no screen for it and the M21.3 permission matrix has no row for it. This is the upward-correction instrument, which the ERP would have raised: M17-35's credit note reasons cover only over-charging, and M17-36 plus WF-100 forbid editing or cancelling an issued invoice, so an invoice that under-charged the customer — the wrong rate-card line, a missed priority surcharge, tax computed intra-State when the place of supply was another State — currently has no lawful correction path at all.
fix:
Insert this row in §10.1 immediately after the Credit Note row:

| **Debit Note number** | `DVM/D/<FY4>/<4>` | `DVM/D/2627/0006` | Financial year | Accounts, Unit Incharge, and the customer | **Gap-free and statutory.** Must reference the invoice number and date it adjusts. Raised only where the taxable value or the tax charged on an issued invoice was **less** than what is payable. |

In the same section replace "Only five series are length-constrained — invoice, bill of supply, advance receipt voucher, refund voucher and credit note." with "Only six series are length-constrained — invoice, bill of supply, advance receipt voucher, refund voucher, credit note and debit note.", and in WF-99 replace "invoice, bill of supply, advance receipt voucher, refund voucher, credit note, money receipt" with "invoice, bill of supply, advance receipt voucher, refund voucher, credit note, debit note, money receipt".

Then insert this row after M17-35 in parts/section_4_functional_support.md:

| M17-35a | [MUST] | The system shall support a **debit note** referencing the original invoice number and date, for the case where the taxable value or the tax charged on that invoice was **less** than what is payable, with a reason from a controlled list (rate applied wrongly — under-charged; priority surcharge omitted; quantity under-billed; tax component computed wrongly; place of supply corrected; other with text) and an approver. It shall carry the same statutory fields, the same sixteen-character financial-year series rule and the same frozen-file rule as the tax invoice (M17-27, M17-28, M17-39), and shall increase the balance on the customer ledger (M17-21). An issued invoice shall never be edited to correct an under-charge; the debit note is the only instrument, as the credit note is the only instrument for an over-charge under M17-36. | Under-bill an invoice by applying the wrong rate-card line, then attempt to edit the issued invoice; refused, with the debit note route offered. Raise the debit note; it references the invoice number and date, takes the next number in its own series, and the customer ledger balance increases by the difference. |

Finally add a row `| Debit note | – | – | – | R | A | R | C | – | – | R own |` to the M21.3 permission matrix beside "Credit note / refund voucher", and a "Debit Note" line to the M17.1 screen table.

locator: §25.2 Transaction tables — `txn_receipt_allocation`
quote: | `txn_receipt_allocation` | Which receipt settles which invoice or advance — supports part payments and running accounts. | `receipt_id`, `invoice_id`, `amount DECIMAL(14,2)` | `id` | both | — | `invoice_id` |
problem: The table can only allocate a receipt to an invoice. M17-13b [MUST] requires the opposite: applying an advance to an order "shall be recorded as a row in the 'Applied to orders' child table of the originating advance Payment", and the M17.6 field table defines that child table as "order, amount applied". An advance is taken before any invoice exists — that is what makes it an advance — so with `invoice_id` as the only target there is nowhere to record the application, and M17-13b's acceptance check ("Post one advance of Rs 10,000 and consume it across three orders; the customer ledger is correct at each step, exactly one Payment record exists") cannot be built on this schema. The shape is a leftover of the withdrawn design, where the ERP held the running account and the LIMS only needed to know which invoice a receipt settled; §25.2 accordingly names no customer-ledger table at all, and M17-21, M17-46 and M20-30 ("the totals reconcile to the customer ledgers") have no storage behind them.
fix:
Replace the row with:

| `txn_receipt_allocation` | Which receipt settles which invoice **or which order**, and what remains unapplied — supports part payments, advances taken before any invoice exists, and the running account. Exactly one of `invoice_id` and `order_id` is set: `invoice_id` where the receipt settles an issued document, `order_id` where an advance is applied to work not yet invoiced (M17-13b). Unallocated receipt amount is the customer's advance balance and is never a row here. | `receipt_id`, `invoice_id BIGINT NULL`, `order_id BIGINT NULL`, `amount DECIMAL(14,2)`, `allocated_at`, `allocated_by_user_id` | `id` | `receipt_id`, `invoice_id`, `order_id` | — | `invoice_id`; `order_id`; `receipt_id` |

and add, in §25.6 or §25.2's notes: "`CHECK ((invoice_id IS NULL) <> (order_id IS NULL))` — an allocation targets an invoice or an order, never both and never neither."

Extend DB-37 to read: "A receipt's allocations cannot exceed the receipt amount, and an invoice's paid amount cannot exceed its total. | `CHECK (paid_amount <= total_amount)` plus a trigger summing `txn_receipt_allocation` (over both invoice and order allocations) against `txn_receipt.amount`."

Add one sentence to the §25.2 preamble: "**The customer ledger of M17-21 is a derived view, not a table:** it is `txn_invoice` (charges, credit notes and debit notes) plus `txn_receipt` (money in and, under M17-33a, money out) plus `txn_receipt_allocation` (what has been applied to what), ordered by document date. There is deliberately no stored balance column, because a stored balance and its underlying documents cannot be made to disagree if the balance is never stored."

locator: M21.11 Configuration and feature switches introduced by this document
quote: The register covers M10 to M22.
problem: The register claims to cover M10 to M22 and to be "the single place an assessor looks for every value the laboratory can change without a developer", but it contains no switch for the M22 interface itself. Four requirements branch on a configuration state the document never names or defaults: M12-20 ("Where an external accounting system has been configured under M22, the approved indent shall also be transmitted to it"), the M12.3 item-master field ("Populated by the M22 interface where it is enabled; empty otherwise"), M21-72a ("Where the optional interface in M22 is ever enabled") and M22-17 itself ("The LIMS shall run with the integration switched off entirely"). The whole standalone position rests on that off state, and it is the one setting in the money and stock area with no configuration key, no recorded default and nothing for the go-live checklist or an assessor to inspect.
fix:
Insert this row in the M21.11 table immediately after the `returns_filed_upto` row:

| `external_accounting_interface_enabled` | **Off**, and off at delivery | M22-17, M22-01, M12-20, M12.3 item master, M21-72a. While Off, no outbound accounting message is produced and no external reference is required on any screen (M22-19); the external-reference fields on the customer, item, invoice and asset records stay empty and hand-editable. Turning it On is a change subject to M21-57 change control and requires the ownership table of M22.1 to have been agreed in writing first. |

locator: WF-3 (§ workflow rules), and the same phrase at §11 Proforma entity note and §10.1 Proforma row
quote: | **WF-3** | [MUST] | A Quotation is an estimate only. It never posts to accounts, never allots an invoice number, and carries a validity date. | Issue a quotation. No entry appears in any invoice or receipt register. |
problem: "Posts to accounts" is ledger-posting language from the withdrawn design, where issued documents were pushed into the ERP to be posted. The general ledger is now out of scope and stays with the accounts wing (N2, M17 ownership note, M22.1), so nothing in this software posts to accounts and the negative statement implies a posting mechanism that other documents supposedly use. The phrase appears three times, all about the quotation and the proforma, and each time the thing actually meant is that the document creates no receivable and no entry in the customer ledger.
fix:
Replace WF-3 with:

| **WF-3** | [MUST] | A Quotation is an estimate only. It creates no charge on the customer ledger, never allots an invoice number, and carries a validity date. | Issue a quotation. No entry appears in the customer ledger, the invoice register or the receipt register. |

At §11, replace "It creates no receivable, posts nothing to accounts, and is an **estimate**" with "It creates no receivable and no entry on the customer ledger, and is an **estimate**". In the §10.1 Proforma / advance demand row, replace "Not a tax document, so no length limit. Never posts to accounts." with "Not a tax document, so no length limit. A demand only: it creates no charge on the customer ledger and no entry in the invoice register."

locator: M12.4 Field table — Consumable Lot Record
quote: | Purchase order / indent reference | Text or link | Yes where purchased | |
problem: The lot record captures the supplier, the indent reference and the certificate of analysis, but nothing about the commercial document the material actually arrived on and nothing about price. Under M22.1 the external system was 'Master of value' and sent 'item identity and cost' to the LIMS, so the purchase facts were never specified here. With that system withdrawn, an assessor tracing a reagent lot back to its supplier can reach the certificate of analysis but cannot reach the bill it came on, and the laboratory has no record of what any reagent cost — which M12-28's consumption report and M12-20's estimated value both silently assume exists.
fix:
Insert these four rows into M12.4 immediately after '| Purchase order / indent reference | Text or link | Yes where purchased | |':

| Supplier's invoice / bill number | Text | Yes where purchased | The commercial document the material arrived on. A lot received without purchase records the source in Remarks under M12.6 rule 7 |
| Supplier's invoice / bill date | Date | Yes where purchased | |
| Purchase rate per unit | Amount | Yes where purchased | As billed, exclusive of tax |
| Lot value as received | Amount | System-computed | Quantity received x purchase rate. A stores figure copied from the supplier's bill, not an accounting valuation: no costing method, revaluation or ledger posting is computed anywhere in this system |
| Purchase document file | File upload | Yes where purchased | The scanned bill or cash memo, held with the lot alongside the certificate of analysis |

And add this requirement to M12.2 after M12-32:

| M12-33 | [MUST] | The system shall record, for every purchased lot, **what was bought, from whom, on what document and at what price**: the supplier, the supplier's invoice or bill number and date, the purchase rate per unit and the resulting lot value, and shall retain the scanned purchase document with the lot alongside the certificate of analysis. These are facts copied from documents the laboratory holds. The system shall **not** compute a costing method, a stock revaluation or any ledger posting; those stay with the unit's accounts wing, which keeps the books. | Receive a lot against a supplier's bill; the Consumable Lot Register and the lot card show the supplier, the bill number and date, the rate and the value, with the scanned bill attached; searching that bill number finds the lot and, through M12-12, every test that used it. |

quote: The system shall hold **asset and depreciation fields** for the parent institute's asset register: purchase order reference, supplier, invoice number and date, capitalised cost, date put to use, funding source or scheme, asset classification, expected useful life, depreciation method and rate, accumulated depreciation, book value, physical verification date and outcome, condemnation reference.
problem: The requirement still names the parent institute's asset register as the thing being fed, and demands depreciation method, depreciation rate, accumulated depreciation and book value — figures nobody in this system can maintain once the general ledger is out of scope. It contradicts M22.1 head-on, which states that the financial asset register 'with its capitalised cost and depreciation' is 'not held here in any configuration', and contradicts N4 in Part A, which keeps capitalisation and depreciation with the accounts wing. A developer reading M11-28 and M11.3 will build depreciation columns the specification elsewhere forbids.
fix:
Replace the whole M11-28 row with:

| M11-28 | [SHOULD] | The system shall hold a **working asset record** for each instrument — what it is, what it cost, where it came from and whether it is still fit to hold: purchase indent or order reference, supplier, supplier's invoice number and date, purchase cost, date put to use, warranty start and end, funding source or scheme, asset classification, expected useful life, physical verification date and outcome, condemnation order reference, disposal date and disposal value. These are facts copied from documents the laboratory holds, and calibration planning, replacement planning and traceability need them. The system shall **not** compute or store depreciation method, depreciation rate, accumulated depreciation or book value: depreciation accounting and the financial fixed-asset register stay with the unit's accounts wing and the parent institute, outside this software (N4, M22.1). The record shall print as an asset card the accounts wing can use, and shall be exportable through the dormant interface in M22 should an accounting system ever be adopted. | The Working Asset Record tab prints an asset card containing every listed field, and the same data is available as an export file. No depreciation, accumulated-depreciation or book-value field exists anywhere in the interface or the schema. |

locator: M11.3 Field table — Equipment Master, Asset tab paragraph
quote: depreciation method, depreciation rate, accumulated depreciation, book value as at date, last physical verification date, verification outcome, condemnation order reference, disposal date, disposal value.
problem: This is the field list a developer will actually build from, and it still spells out four accounting fields — depreciation method, depreciation rate, accumulated depreciation and book value — that require a general ledger behind them. It also opens with 'capitalised cost', which is an accounting term of art for a figure the accounts wing determines, not a purchase price the laboratory can copy off a bill.
fix:
Replace the whole paragraph beginning 'Asset tab (see M11-28):' with:

Working asset record tab (see M11-28): purchase indent or order reference, supplier, supplier's invoice number, invoice date, purchase cost, date put to use, warranty start, warranty end, funding source or scheme name, asset class, expected useful life (years), last physical verification date, verification outcome, condemnation order reference, disposal date, disposal value. There is deliberately no depreciation method, depreciation rate, accumulated depreciation or book-value field: those belong to the financial fixed-asset register, which stays with the unit's accounts wing and the parent institute and is outside this system's scope (N4, M22.1).

quote: Where an external accounting system has been configured under M22, the approved indent shall also be transmitted to it, and shall queue and retry while that system is unreachable.
problem: A [MUST] requirement carries a transmit-and-retry leg to a system that does not exist, and its acceptance check ends 'With the M22 interface enabled, it also appears in the outbound queue and, on success, carries the external purchase-requisition number back' — a purchase sync that cannot be executed at go-live, against machinery OPEN-Q-D35 forbids building. Worse is what the ERP was carrying and nobody replaced: the external purchase-requisition number coming back was the return leg. Today the indent is printed and then falls off the end of the specification. There is no record of who it was handed to, no state, no worklist, and no way to enter the sanction or purchase order reference the accounts wing supplies — which M12.4 then makes mandatory on goods receipt ('Purchase order / indent reference ... Yes where purchased').
fix:
Replace the whole M12-20 row with:

| M12-20 | [MUST] | The system shall raise a **purchase indent** listing items, quantities, required-by date, technical acceptance criteria per item, suggested supplier and estimated value, and route it for Lab In-Charge approval. On approval it shall **print for hand-over to the unit's accounts wing**, which runs the procurement chain outside this software (N3). The system shall record the hand-over — date, the officer it was given to, and a scan of the receipted copy where one is returned — and shall allow the Store Keeper to enter, against that indent, the **sanction or purchase order reference** the accounts wing supplies, so that a goods receipt has a purchase document to name. An indent shall carry a state — Draft, Approved, Handed over, Ordered (reference recorded), Received, Closed, Cancelled — and shall stay on an open-indent worklist until it is closed, so that a request nobody acted on is visible rather than forgotten. Where an external accounting system is ever configured under M22 the approved indent may additionally be transmitted to it; that path is switched off, and is neither built nor tested at go-live (M22-17, OPEN-Q-D35). | Approve an indent; it prints, the hand-over is recorded with a date and a named officer, and it appears on the open-indent worklist. Enter the purchase order reference the accounts wing returns; receiving a lot against that indent offers the reference automatically. Close the indent; it leaves the worklist. No step in the test requires an external system. |

Add the matching table to §25.2 of Part E: `txn_purchase_indent` / `txn_purchase_indent_line` (`unit_id`, `indent_no`, `raised_by_personnel_id`, `raised_on`, `required_by DATE`, `approved_by_personnel_id`, `approved_at`, `handed_over_on DATE`, `handed_over_to`, `handover_attachment_id`, `sanction_or_po_ref`, `po_dated DATE`, `state` / `indent_id`, `line_no`, `consumable_id`, `qty`, `uom_id`, `acceptance_criteria TEXT`, `suggested_supplier_id`, `estimated_value`).

locator: M12.6 rule 9
quote: None exists at present, so the LIMS carries both the quantity and the value of what is in store, which is what a stock register needs
problem: The rule promises a stock value the specification never delivers: no field in M12.4 holds a price, no requirement in M12.2 records one, `mst_consumable_lot` has no cost column, and neither M20-06 (Reagent and Consumable Register) nor M20-29 (Stock position and consumption) prints a value. The sentence is left over from the position where the external system supplied cost. As written it also over-claims in the other direction — 'the value of what is in store' reads as a stock valuation, which is a costing exercise that only makes sense with a ledger behind it.
fix:
Replace the whole of rule 9 with:

9. **Stock value, and how far it goes.** No external accounting system exists, so nothing outside this software holds a figure for what is in store. The LIMS therefore records, per lot, the price it was bought at and the document it was bought on (M12-33), and the stock position report of M20-29 shows quantity and that recorded value side by side. It goes no further: the system runs **no costing method, no stock revaluation and no ledger posting**. Those follow from the movements and stay with the unit's accounts wing, which keeps the books. If an accounting system is ever adopted it becomes the system of record for money value, and the LIMS remains the system of record for **fitness for use** — quarantine, acceptance, expiry, blocking. The two must not both decide whether a lot may be used. See M22.

And extend M20-06 and M20-29 to carry the recorded purchase rate and lot value as columns.

locator: M11, opening paragraph
quote: It is actually two registers that happen to describe the same physical objects: a **money register** for the parent institute's asset and depreciation records, and a **measurement control register** for calibration and traceability. This module builds both and keeps them linked.
problem: The module's framing sentence still says it builds a money register for somebody else's asset and depreciation records. It is the sentence M11-28, M11.3 and the M11.1 screen list all descend from, and it directs the reader to a register the specification elsewhere says stays with the accounts wing. Depreciation records are outside this system's scope; the laboratory keeps a working record of the object, not an accounting one.
fix:
Replace both sentences with:

It is actually two registers that happen to describe the same physical objects: a **working asset record** — what the instrument is, what it cost, who supplied it, where it stands and whether it is still fit to hold — and a **measurement control register** for calibration and traceability. This module builds both and keeps them linked. It does not build an accounting asset register: capitalisation, depreciation and book value stay with the unit's accounts wing and the parent institute, outside this software (N4, M22.1).

locator: § Entity glossary, Equipment
quote: The fixed-asset register (cost, supplier, depreciation, physical verification, condemnation) and the metrological control register (range, interval, calibration result, correction factors, out-of-service status) are two different registers with two different owners.
problem: The glossary hands cost, supplier, physical verification and condemnation to a fixed-asset register with a different owner. Three of those four are now held by this system: M11-28 requires supplier and purchase cost, M11-29 requires the annual physical verification run with Lab In-Charge sign-off, and M11.5 makes Condemned a state of the equipment record with a condemnation order reference. Only depreciation and capitalisation sit elsewhere. A reader taking this entry at face value would build none of M11-28 or M11-29.
fix:
Replace the sentence with:

This system keeps a **working asset record** — supplier, purchase document, cost, date put to use, useful life, physical verification, condemnation reference — alongside the **metrological control register** (range, interval, calibration result, correction factors, out-of-service status). What it does not keep is the financial fixed-asset register: capitalisation, depreciation and book value stay with the unit's accounts wing and the parent institute, outside this software. quote: The system shall provide a **manual override entry** for every ERP-supplied reference — invoice number, receipt number, asset number, purchase order number — so that a value can be typed in. A developer implementing M22-19 literally puts an editable invoice-number field on the invoice screen, which breaks rule 46(b) consecutiveness and the series register of WF-102. This does **not** extend to the tax invoice number, the bill of supply number, the advance receipt voucher number, the refund voucher number, the credit note number or the money receipt number: those are allotted by this system's own locked counter under WF-97, WF-98 and DB-08, are gap-free under WF-99, and are **never typed in by a user** — today, or after any interface is ever commissioned. | Save each record carrying an external reference with that reference left blank; accepted. Then look for a way to type the invoice number: there is no such field, and the number shown is the one the counter allotted. |

locator: M22-02 (line 1780); same defect in M22-08 and M22-13; assumption table M22.3 (lines 1804-1813)
quote: Send the same invoice twice with the same key; the ERP holds one invoice.
problem: This acceptance check tests the unseen system, not this one. An idempotency key only prevents a duplicate if the receiver honours it, and M22.3 — the checklist that exists precisely to list what must be learned about whatever system is eventually named — has eight rows and none of them covers it. The same gap sits under M22-08 ("receipts in the ERP with no LIMS match; stock quantity differences" needs read access to the far side's receipts and stock, a capability no assumption row claims) and M22-13 ("the previous version is still accepted for the configured period" is the far side's behaviour, not ours). fix:
Add three rows to the M22.3 table, after row 8:

| 9 | The system honours an idempotency key supplied by the caller, so a retried message cannot create a second invoice, receipt or indent on its side | M22-02's acceptance check cannot be run at all. Deduplication moves to this side — hold the message, query the far side for the record, send only if it is absent — and the reconciliation report of M22-08 becomes the only guard against a duplicate invoice in what is, on our side, a gap-free statutory series |
| 10 | The system can be **read** as well as written: its receipts, its customer records, its item master and its stock balances can be listed through the same interface | M22-08 shrinks to a one-way check — it can list what this system sent and never got an acknowledgement for, and nothing else. Every other mismatch then surfaces only when a person compares two printouts |
| 11 | The system tolerates a message carrying a schema version, and does not fail on a version it does not recognise | M22-13 cannot be honoured from this side alone. The transition period becomes a scheduled cut-over — both systems changed on the same day with the interface stopped in between — and M22-14's test becomes mandatory rather than prudent |

locator: §25.1 preamble (line 438); columns at lines 446, 465, 468 and 511; M22-07 (section_4 line 1785)
quote: `is_provisional BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false`, `erp_customer_id`, `is_active`
problem: Four `erp_` columns survive in the schema — `mst_customer.erp_customer_id`, `mst_consumable.erp_item_id`, `mst_equipment.erp_asset_id`, `txn_invoice.erp_invoice_id` — with nothing anywhere in §25 saying they are dormant placeholders for a system that does not exist. Keeping them is the right call, but unlabelled they read as live foreign keys, and the first developer to see one will look for the process that populates it. They also disagree with M22-07, which names six identifiers: `erp_receipt_id` and `erp_employee_id` appear in the requirement but in no table. And no table carries the "last-synchronised timestamp" M22-07 also demands, which is correct today but leaves the requirement and the schema visibly out of step.
fix:
Add as a third paragraph of the §25 preamble, after the sentence ending "...with `p` total digits and `s` after the point.":

**Four columns are dormant and deliberately kept.** `mst_customer.erp_customer_id`, `mst_consumable.erp_item_id`, `mst_equipment.erp_asset_id` and `txn_invoice.erp_invoice_id` exist so that an external accounting system, if one is ever mandated, can be linked without a schema change to four large tables. While M22 is switched off — which is the only state this system is built and validated in — they are nullable, carry no foreign key and no constraint, are written by nothing and read by nothing. They are the only four: the `erp_receipt_id`, the `erp_employee_id` and the last-synchronised timestamp that M22-07 also names are **not** created now, and arrive in the migration that commissions the interface, if one ever is.

But ARC-14 is the **operative** standalone-architecture rule, [MUST], the one that says the system owns its customer master, numbering, invoices, receipts and stock outright; and ARC-15 is the [MUST] against proprietary managed-service lock-in. and add to the exclusion paragraph that follows: "ARC-13 is the single architecture rule Phase 1 does not have to satisfy, because it is not operative: there is no accounting package to build inside, and the rule becomes live only if somebody proposes one."

locator: M22.1 ownership table, row "New customer created at the laboratory counter" (line 1747)
quote: | **New customer created at the laboratory counter** | Master, eventually | Creates a provisional record | LIMS → ERP, then ERP → LIMS to confirm | On acceptance of the first order | The provisional customer works fully in the LIMS with a temporary reference; the ERP identifier is filled in when the push succeeds; **sample receipt is never blocked** |
problem: "Provisional" is a settled word in this document with a different meaning. M1-13 and `mst_customer.is_provisional` define a provisional customer as a walk-in created from name, mobile and category alone, against whom no tax invoice may be issued until the State is present. M22.1 reuses the same word for a complete customer record that merely lacks an external identifier — and today every customer record lacks one, because there is no external system. §8.3 requires exactly one word per concept, and this table exists specifically to stop two records of the same thing drifting apart.
fix: | **New customer created at the laboratory counter** | Master, eventually | **Master today; creates the definitive customer record** | LIMS → ERP, then ERP → LIMS to confirm | On acceptance of the first order | The customer record works fully in the LIMS with no external identifier at all; the identifier is filled in when the push succeeds; **sample receipt is never blocked**. This is **not** the `is_provisional` record of M1-13, which means something else entirely — a walk-in whose own details are not yet complete — and the two must never be conflated in the schema or on screen |

quote: The integration shall be **tested against an ERP upgrade** before the upgrade goes live in production, and the test shall be part of the change-control record in M21-57.
problem: As worded this is a [MUST] on this project that this project cannot satisfy on its own: it requires notice of somebody else's upgrade, from somebody who does not exist and who, per OPEN-Q40, has given no such commitment ("who maintains it, and will they commit to a stable interface and to notifying this project before an upgrade?"). The acceptance check — "An ERP upgrade is recorded in the change register with an integration test result" — is a record of the far side's behaviour. Rewriting it to bind only what this side controls, and to name the written commitment as a precondition, makes it a real requirement rather than an aspiration.
fix: | M22-14 | [MUST] | Before any upgrade of the external system goes live in production, the integration shall be tested against the upgraded version in staging, and the result recorded in the Change Control Register of M21-57. **This binds this project's side only, and it depends on notice that nobody has yet undertaken to give (OPEN-Q40): if an interface is ever commissioned, a named contact and a written commitment to give notice before an upgrade shall be obtained first and held with the interface's configuration record. Without that commitment the interface is run on the assumption that it may break without warning, and the reconciliation report of M22-08 is the detector.** | The change register holds an entry for the upgrade naming the version tested against and the outcome, and the interface configuration record names the contact who gave the notice. |
